subject: Geography
description: Highest peaks, longest ranges, fold vs block, Andes, Rockies, Alps, Himalayas

questions.stem: The world's HIGHEST peak (8,848.86 m) and its location:

options.option_text: K2 — Karakoram
Mount Everest (Sagarmatha / Chomolungma) — Mahalangur Himal of the Himalayas, Nepal-China (Tibet) border
Kanchenjunga — Sikkim-Nepal
Mont Blanc — Alps

questions.explanation: Mount Everest — height 8,848.86 m (revised from 8,848 m by joint Nepal-China survey, December 2020). Border peak — Sagarmatha (Nepali, head in the sky) / Chomolungma (Tibetan, mother goddess). Named after Sir George Everest (Surveyor General of India 1830-43). First confirmed summit — Edmund Hillary + Tenzing Norgay, 29 May 1953. K2 (Karakoram, Pakistan-China) — 8,611 m, 2nd highest, technically harder. Kanchenjunga — 8,586 m, India's HIGHEST peak (Sikkim-Nepal). Mont Blanc — Alps, only 4,807 m. 14 peaks > 8,000 m globally — all in Himalaya-Karakoram.

questions.stem: The LONGEST mountain range above sea level (~7,000 km along S America's western edge) is the:

options.option_text: Himalayas
Andes — runs through 7 countries (Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile, Argentina)
Rockies
Atlas

questions.explanation: Andes — longest continental range, ~7,000 km, S American Pacific coast. Highest peak — Aconcagua (Argentina, 6,961 m, highest outside Asia + tallest in Western Hemisphere). Born from convergence of Nazca + South American plates. Many active volcanoes (Cotopaxi, Chimborazo, Llaullaillaco). Longest UNDERWATER mountain range — the Mid-Atlantic Ridge (~16,000 km, mostly submerged). Rockies — ~4,800 km, N America. Himalayas — ~2,400 km only. Tallest mountain measured base-to-summit — Mauna Kea (Hawaii, 10,200 m from ocean floor).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Himalayas are an example of:

options.option_text: Block (fault) mountains
Fold mountains (formed by collision of Indian + Eurasian plates ~50 Ma)
Volcanic mountains
Residual / dome mountains

questions.explanation: Fold mountains — sedimentary layers on the seabed get crumpled when continental plates collide. Indian plate began separating from Africa-Antarctica ~150 Ma, drifted north at ~15 cm/yr. Collided with Eurasian plate ~50 Ma — Tethys Sea closed; sediments piled up to form Himalayas. Still rising ~5 mm/year! Other fold mtns: Andes, Alps, Atlas, Urals, Rockies. BLOCK mountains — rift / horst-graben (Vosges, Rhine valley). VOLCANIC — Mount Fuji, Vesuvius, Kilimanjaro. RESIDUAL — Aravallis (oldest fold mtn, now eroded to remnants). DOME — Black Hills (Dakota).

questions.stem: The HIGHEST mountain in Africa, also a free-standing volcano:

options.option_text: Mount Kenya
Mount Kilimanjaro (5,895 m, in Tanzania) — dormant volcano
Mount Ras Dashen (Ethiopia)
Mount Stanley (Rwenzori)

questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro — Tanzania, 5,895 m. Stratovolcano with three cones (Kibo, Mawenzi, Shira). Largest free-standing mountain (rises ~5 km from surrounding plain). Snow-capped summit (the icecap is shrinking due to climate change — could disappear by 2040). Mount Kenya — 2nd highest in Africa, 5,199 m. Other notable peaks: Mt Damavand (Iran, 5,610 m, highest in Middle East); Vinson Massif (Antarctica, 4,892 m); Mt Kosciuszko (Australia, 2,228 m, highest in Australia mainland; 'Seven Summits' challenge sometimes uses Mt Carstensz Pyramid in Indonesia at 4,884 m as the Oceania peak).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: K2 (the world's 2nd highest peak) is in which mountain range?

options.option_text: Himalayas
Karakoram (Pakistan-administered Kashmir / Xinjiang border)
Alps
Hindu Kush

questions.explanation: K2 (Mt Godwin-Austen / Chhogori) — 8,611 m, in the Karakoram range. India claims it as part of its territory (Pak-occupied Kashmir, Gilgit-Baltistan). 'K2' from the British Survey of India numbering — K1 = Masherbrum, K3 = Broad Peak. First summited 1954 (Italian expedition Lacedelli + Compagnoni). One of the deadliest 8000ers — climber fatality rate ~25%. Karakoram = 4 of the 14 eight-thousanders (K2, Gasherbrum I, II, Broad Peak). Plus Nanga Parbat (Himalaya, Gilgit-Baltistan), Kanchenjunga, Lhotse, Makalu, Annapurna … all 14 are in Pakistan, India, Nepal, China, with 8 in Nepal.

questions.stem: The Aravalli range — running ~700 km from Gujarat through Rajasthan to Delhi — is famous as:

options.option_text: World's youngest mountain range
One of the oldest fold mountain ranges on Earth (~3.5 billion years)
Active volcanic chain
Block mountains

questions.explanation: Aravallis — formed in the Proterozoic (~3.5 Ga, earlier estimates 700 Ma), ancient Precambrian fold mountains. Have eroded substantially — current highest peak Guru Shikhar (Mt Abu, 1,722 m). Function as a critical biogeographic barrier — separating Thar Desert from Gangetic plains. Acts as 'green wall' protecting NCR. Mining + sand quarrying in Rajasthan — major environmental damage; SC banned mining in protected stretches. Compare Western Ghats (~150 Ma, much younger), Eastern Ghats (similar age to Aravallis but different orogeny), Himalayas (~50 Ma, youngest).

questions.stem: Match peak with continent — INCORRECT pairing:

options.option_text: Mount Aconcagua — South America
Mount Denali (formerly McKinley) — North America
Mount Vinson Massif — Africa
Mount Kosciuszko — Australia (mainland)

questions.explanation: Vinson Massif (4,892 m) is in ANTARCTICA (Ellsworth Mountains) — not Africa. Africa's highest is Kilimanjaro. The 'Seven Summits' (highest peak on each continent): Asia — Everest (8,849); S America — Aconcagua (6,961); N America — Denali (6,190; renamed back from McKinley in 2025); Africa — Kilimanjaro (5,895); Europe — Elbrus (5,642, Russia); Antarctica — Vinson Massif (4,892); Oceania — Carstensz Pyramid (4,884) or Kosciuszko (2,228, Aus mainland) — debated. Reinhold Messner's list uses Carstensz; original Bass list uses Kosciuszko.

questions.stem: Which peak holds the distinction of being the highest point in both the Alps and Western Europe?

options.option_text: Monte Rosa, the highest summit along the Swiss-Italian border
Mont Blanc, straddling the French-Italian border near Chamonix
Matterhorn, the famous pyramid peak on the Swiss-Italian frontier
Jungfrau, a prominent summit in the Bernese Alps of Switzerland

questions.explanation: Mont Blanc (4,808 m) is the highest summit in both the Alps and Western Europe, located on the French-Italian border near Chamonix. Monte Rosa (4,634 m) is the second-highest Alpine peak and the highest point entirely within Switzerland — a frequent distractor — but it ranks below Mont Blanc overall.

questions.stem: The Ural Mountains are conventionally treated as the boundary between two continents. Which pair correctly names those continents?

options.option_text: Europe and Asia, running roughly north-south through Russia
Asia and North America, divided further by the Bering Strait
Europe and Africa, separated mainly by the Mediterranean Sea
Asia and Australia, linked across the Indian Ocean island chain

questions.explanation: The Ural Mountains (~2,500 km, running north to south through Russia) form the conventional geographical boundary between Europe and Asia. Option B describes the Bering Strait (Asia–North America boundary) and Option C describes the Mediterranean Sea (Europe–Africa), both common confusions in exam settings.

questions.stem: The Atlas Mountains traverse three North African countries. Which of the following is NOT among them?

options.option_text: Morocco, where the High Atlas peaks exceed 4,000 metres
Algeria, where the Tell Atlas borders the Mediterranean coast
Egypt, whose terrain is dominated by the Eastern Desert plateau
Tunisia, where the Atlas forms low ranges in the northwest

questions.explanation: The Atlas system extends through Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia. Egypt's relief is defined by desert plateaus, the Nile valley, and the Sinai — the Atlas range does not reach that far east. Libya (just west of Egypt) is also outside the Atlas system, making Egypt the unambiguous correct answer here.

questions.stem: At its northeastern extremity, the Hindu Kush converges with a highland junction sometimes called the 'Roof of the World'. What is this junction known as?

options.option_text: The Karakoram Node, where the K2 massif anchors the ranges
The Pamir Knot, where the Hindu Kush, Karakoram and Tien Shan converge
The Kunlun Hub, linking Tibet's northern ranges to Central Asia
The Wakhan Corridor, a narrow Afghan strip that bridges the ranges

questions.explanation: The Pamir Knot (Pamirs, largely in Tajikistan) is the great highland junction where the Hindu Kush, Karakoram, Kunlun, and Tien Shan ranges radiate outward — earning the 'Roof of the World' title. Option A is tempting because K2 is the most famous Karakoram peak, but the actual convergence node lies in the Pamirs, not at the K2 massif. The Wakhan Corridor is an Afghan geographic strip, not a mountain junction.

questions.stem: Vinson Massif, the highest peak on the Antarctic continent, belongs to which specific mountain range?

options.option_text: The Transantarctic Mountains, which bisect the entire continent
The Sentinel Range within the Ellsworth Mountains in West Antarctica
The Queen Maud Mountains, bordering the Ross Ice Shelf sector
The Prince Charles Mountains located in the Mac Robertson Land area

questions.explanation: Vinson Massif (4,892 m) lies in the Sentinel Range, which is the highest part of the Ellsworth Mountains in West Antarctica. Option A (Transantarctic Mountains) is the most common wrong answer — they are Antarctica's longest and most famous range — but Vinson is geographically separate, situated in Marie Byrd Land / Ellsworth region. Queen Maud and Prince Charles Mountains are in East Antarctica.

questions.stem: Among the 14 globally recognised eight-thousander peaks, exactly how many are situated in the Karakoram range?

options.option_text: Three — K2, Gasherbrum I (Hidden Peak), and Broad Peak alone
Four — K2, Gasherbrum I, Broad Peak, and Gasherbrum II together
Five — the four above plus Nanga Parbat in northern Pakistan
Six — counting Distaghil Sar and Rakaposhi as additional summits

questions.explanation: Exactly 4 of the 14 eight-thousanders are in the Karakoram: K2 (8,611 m), Gasherbrum I/Hidden Peak (8,080 m), Broad Peak (8,051 m), and Gasherbrum II (8,035 m). Option C is the classic trap — Nanga Parbat (8,126 m) is in Pakistan but is geologically the westernmost peak of the Himalayan system, not the Karakoram. Distaghil Sar (7,885 m) and Rakaposhi (7,788 m) are prominent Karakoram peaks but do not exceed 8,000 m.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly pairs a mountain range with the specific tectonic process primarily responsible for its formation?

options.option_text: Rocky Mountains — collision of the North American and Eurasian plates
Andes — subduction of the Nazca Plate beneath the South American Plate
Alps — subduction of the North American Plate under the Eurasian Plate
Ural Mountains — ongoing subduction of the Indian Plate under Eurasia

questions.explanation: The Andes formed through subduction of the oceanic Nazca Plate beneath the continental South American Plate — a textbook convergent margin. Option A is wrong: the Rockies formed via the Laramide Orogeny (subduction of the Farallon Plate under North America, not the Eurasian Plate). Option C is wrong: the Alps formed through collision of the African and Eurasian plates, not the North American Plate. Option D is wrong: the Urals are ancient collision mountains (Laurussia–Kazakhstania); the Indian Plate drives the Himalayan system, not the Urals.
